summary: Feed s156_double to IDS is degraded: 10.4% TCP packet loss (genuine drops, not slicing) and 14.8% truncated frames to 192 bytes prevent full payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Genuine packet loss in the visibility path - 310 of 2985 TCP packets (10.4%) show gaps in TCP sequence. Check ruled out slicing as cause by measuring IP length, so drops are real. Most likely SPAN/mirror oversubscription or packet broker buffer drops under burst, not tool overload (tool_overload healthy) or slicing.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot reassemble TCP streams, misses signatures across missing segments, creates false negatives and broken flow state; detection coverage severely reduced.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless, line-rate copy vs SPAN which drops when oversubscribed; eliminates broker/SPAN buffer loss before IDS. If TAP already in use, add aggregation/filtering to reduce burst loss.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker slicing enabled - 456 of 3077 frames (14.8%) cut short, most to 192 bytes snaplen. Broker is truncating payload to save bandwidth/tool capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload (tool profile: needs_full_payload=true) for signature matching and protocol parsing; truncated payload blinds IDS to exploits, malware and C2 in upper layers.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full packet payload for detection; disable slicing or set snaplen >=1518 to forward complete frames to IDS.
